agree.reason: The need is well documented and the reserves commitment is strong, but Marisol had to chase the last report for four months, and the draft gives her no concrete reporting commitment, so she may not get past that history.

honest.reason: The draft correctly drops the 'double in the first year' claim the facts cannot support and its arithmetic checks out, but it adds small details the brief never gave: that the produce was 'offered free' and 'grown in this county.'

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are worked out correctly from the brief: about 10 pounds of fresh food per household, under a sixth of the total, 3,000 pounds a month (a 50% increase in summer), 15 pounds per household, more than a quarter of the cost paid from reserves, and most of the savings committed, each put in its strongest true form.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is stated plainly and matches the facts: without the van, the farms offer and the food bank has to say no again. There is no trend data to add, though the draft could have said a year-round fresh-food gain is unknown.

qualification.reason: The commitment to measure results against the 9,000-pound benchmark can be checked, but it gives no report date and no consequence if the target is missed, which matters most for this reader.

objections.reason: The late report is acknowledged with dignity but nothing is offered to fix it, such as a reporting date or a named person responsible, and the draft never addresses how the van will be insured, fuelled and maintained once reserves are down to $11,000.

fit.reason: It is a clearly sectioned project narrative of about 470 words, within the 500-word limit.
